tasks.notes: f(x)=|3+5^(3-x)|-1; since 3+5^(3-x)>3>0 always, f(x)=2+5^(3-x), range = (2,+inf) (option A per key). Answer is an interval/range, not a single number.

tasks.summary_en: Trapezoid: AD=6, BC=12, AC=10, equal angles. |AB|=?
tasks.statement_en: In trapezoid ABCD with bases AB and CD, we have |AD|=6, |BC|=12, |AC|=10, and |\angle ABC|=|\angle CAD| [Figure: trapezoid with D and C on the top base, A and B on the bottom base; diagonal AC=10; angle alpha marked at vertex A (angle CAD) and at vertex B (angle ABC)]. Then the length of base AB of this trapezoid equals: A. |AB|=18, B. |AB|=20, C. |AB|=22, D. |AB|=24
tasks.notes: Equal angles + CD||AB give triangle ACD ~ triangle BAC (AA), so AD/BC=AC/AB => 6/12=10/AB => AB=20, matches option B.

tasks.summary_pl: Ostrosłup o rów. krawędziach: cosinus kąta nachylenia ściany
tasks.summary_en: Pyramid with equal edges: cosine of face inclination angle
tasks.statement_en: In a regular quadrilateral pyramid all edges have the same length. It follows that the cosine of the angle of inclination of a lateral face to the plane of the base of this pyramid equals: A. $\frac{\sqrt3}{3}$, B. $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$, C. $\frac12$, D. $\frac13$
tasks.notes: Base side a=lateral edge; apothem=a/2, slant height=a*sqrt3/2 (from H=a/sqrt2), cos(angle)=apothem/slant height=1/sqrt3=sqrt3/3, matches option A.

tasks.statement_en: The limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{-7n^3+3n}{1+2n+3n^2+4n^5}$ is equal to: A. $-\infty$, B. $-\frac{7}{4}$, C. 0, D. $+\infty$
tasks.notes: Denominator degree (5) exceeds numerator degree (3), so the limit is 0, matches option C.

tasks.summary_en: Infinite geometric seq: q=a1, sum=12. Find a1
tasks.statement_en: An infinite geometric sequence $(a_n)$ is defined for $n\ge1$, in which the common ratio equals the first term, and the sum of all the terms of this sequence equals 12. Compute the first term of this sequence. Code in sequence the first three digits after the decimal point of the obtained result.
tasks.notes: a1/(1-a1)=12 => a1=12/13=0.923076923..., coded digits 9,2,3 (matches key's second digit row). [verified: ok: a1/(1-a1)=12 -> a1=12/13 (|q|<1); key codes 9,2,3.]

tasks.statement_en: Random events $A,B\subset\Omega$ are given such that $P(A)=\frac{2}{7}$ and $P(A\cup B)=\frac{3}{5}$. Compute $P(B\setminus A)$, where the event $B\setminus A$ denotes the difference of events B and A. Code in sequence the first three digits after the decimal point of the decimal expansion of the obtained result.
tasks.notes: P(B\A)=P(A union B)-P(A)=3/5-2/7=11/35=0.314285714..., coded digits 3,1,4 (matches key's first digit row).
Solve |x-1|*|x-2| >= x-1; solution set x in (-inf,1] union [3,+inf). Answer is a set, not a single number.

tasks.statement_en: A sequence $(a_n)$ is defined for every integer $n\ge1$, in which $a_4=4$ and for every $n\ge1$ the equality $a_{n+1}=a_n+n-4$ holds. Compute the first term of this sequence $a_1$ and determine whether this sequence is decreasing.
tasks.notes: Backward from a4=4: a3=5, a2=7, a1=10 (matches key). Second part of the task (is the sequence decreasing - answer: no, since a4=a5=4) is not numeric, so only a1=10 is used as the value.

Solve (2sin x - sqrt3)(2sin x + 1) > 0 on (0, 2pi); solution x in (7pi/6, 11pi/6). Answer is an interval, not a single number.

tasks.statement_en: In a right triangle, the ratio of the difference of the lengths of the legs to the length of the hypotenuse equals $\frac12$. Compute the cosines of the acute angles of this triangle.
tasks.notes: Key gives cos(alpha)=(sqrt7-1)/4, cos(beta)=(sqrt7+1)/4; sum = sqrt7/2 (suma cosinusow).

tasks.statement_en: Compute how many five-digit natural numbers there are in which exactly three digits are odd.

tasks.summary_en: Isosceles triangle: find vertex C (sum of coordinates)
tasks.statement_en: Points $A=(-7,-2)$ and $B=(4,-7)$ are vertices of the base of isosceles triangle ABC, and the altitude dropped from vertex A of this triangle lies on the line with equation $2x+19y+52=0$. Compute the coordinates of vertex C.
tasks.notes: Key computes C=(6,12); sum of coordinates 6+12=18 (suma wspolrzednych).

tasks.summary_pl: Walec o polu $2\pi$: promień i max objętość (suma)
tasks.summary_en: Cylinder with surface area $2\pi$: radius and max volume (sum)
tasks.statement_en: We consider all cylinders whose total surface area equals $2\pi$. Compute the radius of the base of the cylinder that has the greatest volume. State this greatest volume.
tasks.notes: Key derives r=cbrt(1/3), V_max=2*sqrt3*pi/9 via calculus (derivative of V(r)=pi*r-pi*r^3). Sum of the two requested numbers (r + V) = about 1.90256 (r+V, suma promienia i objetosci).
